subject: ddply progress bar only reflects map time, not reduce time

messages.author: 9e1d805a26f6d719
messages.subject: ddply progress bar only reflects map time, not reduce time
parts:
Hi Hadley et al,

I'm working with a relatively complicated ddply operation, one that is
large enough that I want to use the (awesome!) progress bar. But the
progress bar gets to 100% only partially through the ddply call.
Looking at the code, it appears as if the progress bar applies only to
the llply() call, but not to the subsequent list_to_dataframe() call.
In this case, this step takes even longer than the llply step!

So... Is it expected that list_to_dataframe would take so long? If
not, under what circumstances would it? If so, consider "make progress
bar apply to list_to_dataframe" an enhancement request. :)

Thanks!

-Harlan

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: ddply progress bar only reflects map time, not reduce time
parts:
Hi Harlan,

Yup, this is a known problem but unfortunately doesn't have a known
solution. However, in general I'm trying to make list_to_dataframe as
fast as possible, and there should be substantial speed improvements
in the next version.

One thing that can make a big difference is using factors - depending
on the number of factor and split levels, using character vectors can
result in a _big_ speed up.

Hadley
